jordan: Heads-up: bringing up kohlrabi (multilang embed, Mistral-derivative). Quick int4 smoke shows a big drop for ja only. EN/FR look fine. Anyone seen per-lang collapse like this?
michelle: Numbers?
jordan: fp16 baseline recall@1/5/10 -> en 0.84/0.93/0.96, fr 0.78/0.90/0.94, ja 0.72/0.86/0.91.
jordan: int4 (our default symmetric per-tensor calib) -> en 0.82/0.92/0.95, fr 0.75/0.88/0.93, ja 0.50/0.73/0.86 :confounded:
sam: Thats big. First suspects: calibration distribution bias (english-heavy), or per-tensor quant clipping dims important for ja. Also check if export added any post-export ops (norm, transpose).
jordan: We recently added an L2-normalize in the export path for int4 only (to keep serving normalized), fp16 kept as-is. Tokenization changed slightly for ja in upstream tokenizer too.
elaine: Tokenizer shifts can change avg norm per-token, but a 0.22 drop in recall@1 is extreme. Might be quant clipping high-variance dimensions used by japanese tokens.
michelle: Can you share the eval command + a small CSV?
jordan: Ran: ```python eval_embeddings.py --model kohlrabi:int4 --dataset langmix_holdout --metrics recall@1,5,10 --batch-size 32 --normalize True``` Dump CSV: ```model,lang,recall@1,recall@5
kohlrabi-fp16,en,0.84,0.93
kohlrabi-fp16,fr,0.78,0.90
kohlrabi-fp16,ja,0.72,0.86
kohlrabi-int4,en,0.82,0.92
kohlrabi-int4,fr,0.75,0.88
kohlrabi-int4,ja,0.50,0.73```
sam: Quick diagnostics: compare raw dot product magnitudes and normalized cosine for ja between fp16 and int4. If raw mags collapse maybe quant scale wrong; if raw okay but cosine bad maybe zeros/nans introduced. Minimal script: 
```python
import numpy as np
E_q = np.load('q_ja_int4.npy')
E_c = np.load('c_ja_int4.npy')
raw = (E_q @ E_c.T).mean()
from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import cosine_similarity
ns = cosine_similarity(E_q, E_c).mean()
print(raw, ns)
```
jordan: Ran similar quick checks: raw mean for ja int4 ~0.11 vs fp16 raw ~0.34. So magnitudes are suppressed post-quant, not only normalize mismatch.
elaine: That points to calibration/clipping. What calibration dataset did you use? English-heavy?
jordan: Small perf-oriented calib set (english majority). Not balanced.
sam: Try per-channel quant and recalibrate using lang-balanced samples (en,fr,ja). Per-channel often preserves dims with localized ranges.
jordan: Doing that now. Also diffed a few vectors element-wise between fp16 and int4 and saw many dimensions near-zero in int4 where fp16 had significant values.
michelle: Block the canary until we confirm? ops, deploy-bot: @ops confirm hold?
ops: Hold the canary, yes. Dont roll until we confirm multilingual parity.
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled at 23:00 UTC; will pause until manual go.
jordan: Updates after tests (t+40m):
- per-channel int4 w/ old calib -> ja recall@1 = 0.65 (much better)
- per-channel int4 w/ lang-balanced calib -> ja recall@1 = 0.71 (near fp16 0.72)
- disabling post-export L2-normalize made little difference (so not the normalize op)
- tokenization diff accounted for tiny shift only (~0.01 recall)
So root cause: per-tensor symmetric quant + english-heavy calib clipped jap-important dims.
sam: Great catch. Action items: make per-channel quant the default for multilingual models or require lang-stratified calibration. Open a PR with benchmarks.
jordan: Opening PR with artifact links and calibration script: https://git.redwood/kohlrabi/quant-recs/pull/67
michelle: Also add a lang-coverage check to the quant pipeline and a small unit test that runs a few ja queries through calibration.
elaine: Add a note in the model onboarding checklist: if model is multilingual -> per-channel quant + stratified calibration.
jordan: Will update docs + add tests. Thanks all, saved the rollout.
